browser: Chromium 141.0.7390.37 (Playwright's build v1194, the one CI installs), headless, via playwright-core 1.56.1
note: expected_http_error_console_lines are the browser's own log lines for intentionally provoked failures (revision conflicts, a rejected element, refused tokens after simulated and real API restarts, save failure, save conflict, connection resets that drop create responses, a refused token before an unconfirmed create is resent, two failed autosaves, a late autosave reply held until the page moved to a copy, an edit refused after another client moved the session, and a refused token when an edit to a copy reaches a restarted service, read-only storage, a document busy behind a CLI's save lock, save replies the page never got, and a copy whose first reply was dropped and whose check was answered request_in_progress). The storage-feedback steps make documents/ read-only, hold a save lock in a CLI process (detected with a non-blocking flock probe), hold one save reply 11 s past the page's 10 s deadline, drop two save replies with a connection reset after the service answered, and answer a copy first with a dropped connection and then with request_in_progress; they check how many requests the page sent and that all carried one request ID. The steps that make documents/ or drafts/ read-only (read-only storage, the failed autosaves, and the left-open copy) are skipped when running as root, since permissions do not stop root, and are then listed in skipped_steps. edits_while_a_request_is_pending delays transactions by 400 ms. The recovery steps kill the API process with SIGKILL and start a new one. Before a kill that follows a draft discard or a copy, they wait for the page's list read that those trigger: CI run 40652695710 failed once when the kill cut that read off and the development proxy answered it 502 (a test synchronization race; the same sequence exists on main). The simulated-restart step used to fail now and then (#8; 1 of 20 runs on main): a request started just as the step's one-time route was used stalled in the browser, because playwright-core 1.56.1 turns request interception off when the last page route goes away. The smoke now keeps interception on with a context-wide pass-through route, and the step waits for the retried edit's response; see browser-route-race.json. This result: a local run with the Chromium build CI installs, CHEMIFREE_SMOKE_NO_SKIPS=1 and FORCE_COLOR=1; earlier runs with Google Chrome 147 passed 10 of 10 and 5 of 5. Every run writes results.json, build.log, environment.json, requests.log, api.log (--log-requests), and web.log; a failed run also writes failure.png. CI runs it in the browser job; see browser-ci.json.
